cards.explanation: The answer is True. Matthew tells us up front that these are Sadducees “…who say there is no resurrection…” (Matthew 22:23). So before they say a word, we already know where their question is headed. It's like a friend asking for advice when he's already made up his mind, friends.

The answer is to raise up children for his brother. The Sadducees say Moses declared the brother is to marry the widow and raise up offspring for the man who died (Matthew 22:24). The point is children for the brother who had none. Short, simple and right there in the verse.

The answer is his brother. The Sadducees say the first brother married, died without children, and left his wife to his brother (Matthew 22:25). That matches the rule they just quoted from Moses. And it sets the table for the rest of their story.

The answer is which brother will be her husband. The Sadducees ask, “In the resurrection, then, whose wife will she be of the seven?” and add that all of them were married to her (Matthew 22:28). They've lined up seven brothers like dominoes and want Jesus to pick one. Notice the question is built on the idea that she would be married to one of them in the resurrection.

The answer is that they don't know the Scriptures or God's power. Jesus says, “You are mistaken because you do not know the Scriptures or the power of God.” (Matthew 22:29). Two things are named, the Scriptures and God's power. He says it straight, and then He gets to work answering them.

The answer is False. Jesus says people will neither marry nor be given in marriage in the resurrection, and that they will be like the angels in heaven (Matthew 22:30). The Sadducees built their whole puzzle on marriage carrying on, friends. Jesus answers that puzzle in one line.
The answer is what God said to them. Jesus asks, “…have you not read what God said to you…” (Matthew 22:31). He points them to God's own words. And then He quotes them.

The answer is living. Jesus says, “He is not the God of the dead, but of the living.” (Matthew 22:32). He says it after quoting God's words about Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. That's the heart of His answer on whether the dead rise.

The answer is astonished. Matthew writes, “When the crowds heard this, they were astonished at His teaching.” (Matthew 22:33). Seven brothers, a tricky question, and Jesus answers it in a few verses. Jaws on the floor, I'd say, friends.
